question: How many pedestrians were killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes each year from 2013 to 2025?

options.denominator: None; absolute count of pedestrian deaths
options.reason: Bars make it easy to compare the absolute number of deaths across discrete calendar years.
options.interpretation: This answers how many pedestrians were killed in each requested year, with one annual total per bar. Absolute counts are a direct match for the question and allow year-to-year comparisons. It does not explain the circumstances of these deaths or provide population- or traffic-adjusted risk.

options.denominator: None; absolute count of pedestrian deaths
options.reason: A line chart emphasizes how the annual death count changes over time while retaining the values for each year.
options.interpretation: This answers how the annual number of pedestrian deaths changes from 2013 through 2025, and the labeled points give the count for each year. A connected time series is defensible for emphasizing temporal movement in the same calendar-year totals. It does not explain the circumstances of these deaths or provide population- or traffic-adjusted risk.

answer:
The bar chart shows pedestrian deaths of 176 in 2013, 133 in 2014, 133 in 2015, 149 in 2016, 127 in 2017, 123 in 2018, 131 in 2019, 101 in 2020, 132 in 2021, 135 in 2022, 107 in 2023, 124 in 2024, and 119 in 2025.
The line chart shows the same annual counts, highlighting how the total changed over time: 176 in 2013, 133 in 2014, 133 in 2015, 149 in 2016, 127 in 2017, 123 in 2018, 131 in 2019, 101 in 2020, 132 in 2021, 135 in 2022, 107 in 2023, 124 in 2024, and 119 in 2025.
